newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL share index set to test record high - analysts.
newsitem.headline: KL share index set to test record high - analysts.

text.p: The Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange Composite Index, the Malaysian stock market barometer, is set to test its all-time high of 1,332.04 within the first half of the year, analysts said at the weekend.
The record was set on January 5, 1994.
Martin French, managing director of Credit Lyonnais Securities, told a stock market seminar that he expected the Composite Index to reach the 1,300-1,350 level very soon.
"But one should be very careful of investing in a margin...do not be too greedy," he warned.
The index closed on Friday at 1,262.86.
MBf Unit Trust Management chief economist Ghazali Atan said improvement in the country's macroeconomic perspective would provide a favourable backdrop for the local stock market.

"Better short term outlook for the current account, moderating money supply growth rate and moderating interest rates during the first half of the year would be positive for the market," he said. "The ringgit's strength is an added attraction."
Ghazali said worries over valuation and earnings growth of U.S.-listed stocks could also prompt U.S. investors to relocate more funds outside the United States.

PB Securities' head of research, Razani Radzi, said even if the market corrected to 1,180-1,190 should the 1,280 resistance be broken, it should be seen as a buying opportunity for fundamental fund managers.
"Over the year, there will be more good news ahead," he said.
